Typical weight of a whole wheel of chees.Bocconcini (one ball): The name means little mouthfuls in Italian, and these small fresh mozzarella balls are usually sold floating in whey.
Typical weight of a whole wheel of chees.Crottin de Chavignol: This small goat cheese from a Loire village hardens and darkens with age, and is often grilled warm on salads.
Typical weight of a whole wheel of chees.Camembert: Legend credits farmer Marie Harel of Normandy around 1791, and its small wooden box helped it travel and spread.
Typical weight of a whole wheel of chees.Reblochon: In Savoy, farmers once under-milked their cows for the landlord's tax count and then milked again, giving the name meaning to pinch the udder again.
Typical weight of a whole wheel of chees.Edam: Its red wax coat is not only for show, and the cheese keeps well, so it was a staple aboard Dutch ships.
Typical weight of a whole wheel of chees.Brie de Meaux: It was nicknamed the king of cheeses at the Congress of Vienna in 1815, according to a famous story involving Talleyrand.
Typical weight of a whole wheel of chees.Stilton: Only counties in Derbyshire, Leicestershire and Nottinghamshire may make it, and none is allowed in Stilton village itself.
Typical weight of a whole wheel of chees.Pecorino Romano: Made from sheep's milk, it was a ration for Roman legions, and today most is made in Sardinia.
Typical weight of a whole wheel of chees.Parmigiano Reggiano: Banks in Italy accept wheels as collateral for loans, and each is aged at least 12 months before it can be sold.
Typical weight of a whole wheel of chees.Emmental: The holes come from gas released by bacteria during ripening, and the huge wheels are a Swiss alpine cheese icon.

Multi-sport games, by first edition.Far Eastern Championship Games: Held in Manila in 1913, this was Asia's first regional multi-sport event, contested chiefly by the Philippines, China and Japan.
Multi-sport games, by first edition.British Empire Games: Now the Commonwealth Games, it began in Hamilton, Ontario with 11 nations, and its name has changed several times since.
Multi-sport games, by first edition.Maccabiah Games: Often nicknamed the 'Jewish Olympics', this Tel Aviv event brings together Jewish and Israeli athletes from around the world.
Multi-sport games, by first edition.Asian Games: New Delhi hosted the first Asian Games, with 11 nations competing. Today it is the world's second-largest multi-sport event after the Olympics.
Multi-sport games, by first edition.Universiade: Also called the World University Games, it began in Turin and is held every two years for athletes at university level.
Multi-sport games, by first edition.Special Olympics: Eunice Kennedy Shriver began with a backyard summer camp for people with intellectual disabilities. The first Games were held in Chicago.
Multi-sport games, by first edition.World Games: This event features sports outside the Olympic program, such as tug of war, korfball and fistball. It was first held in Santa Clara, California.
Multi-sport games, by first edition.Goodwill Games: Media mogul Ted Turner launched these games in Moscow after the Olympic boycotts of 1980 and 1984 had split the Cold War sports world.
Multi-sport games, by first edition.Youth Olympic Games: Held first in Singapore, these Games are for athletes aged 14 to 18 and mix sports with cultural and education programs.
Multi-sport games, by first edition.Invictus Games: Prince Harry founded these Games for wounded service personnel; the name means 'unconquered', from a poem by William Ernest Henley.

One 1970s classic per year: put them in.M*A*S*H (film): Robert Altman's Korean War black comedy won the Palme d'Or at Cannes and inspired the long-running TV series.
One 1970s classic per year: put them in.Dirty Harry: Clint Eastwood's Do you feel lucky, punk? line made it one of cinema's most quoted.
One 1970s classic per year: put them in.The Godfather: Marlon Brando won an Oscar but declined it, sending Sacheen Littlefeather to protest Hollywood's portrayal of Native Americans.
One 1970s classic per year: put them in.The Sting: It won Best Picture, and its use of Scott Joplin's The Entertainer revived interest in ragtime.
One 1970s classic per year: put them in.Chinatown: Robert Towne's script won an Oscar; Roman Polanski changed the bleak ending over Towne's objections.
One 1970s classic per year: put them in.Jaws: Its mechanical shark, nicknamed Bruce, kept breaking, so Spielberg showed it little, which made it scarier.
One 1970s classic per year: put them in.Taxi Driver: Robert De Niro reportedly improvised You talkin' to me?, and Scorsese's film won the Palme d'Or.
One 1970s classic per year: put them in.Star Wars: Fox executives had little faith, and Lucas took the merchandising rights instead of a larger fee, which later made him rich.
One 1970s classic per year: put them in.Grease: It was the top-grossing film of 1978 in the US, and its soundtrack was a worldwide hit.
One 1970s classic per year: put them in.Apocalypse Now: Coppola's shoot in the Philippines ran far over schedule, a story told in the documentary Hearts of Darkness.

Units of weight.Grain: The grain was once literally a grain of barley or wheat, and it is still the base unit of weight for bullets and gunpowder charges.
Units of weight.Carat: The carat used to be tied to carob seeds, and the same word, spelled karat, now measures gold purity out of 24 parts.
Units of weight.Gram: Originally defined as the weight of a cubic centimetre of water, the gram is the everyday scale unit nearly every country's recipes use.
Units of weight.Dram: The dram is an old apothecary unit, and the same word also became a Scottish term for a small measure of whisky.
Units of weight.Ounce: The ounce abbreviation oz comes from Italian onza; 16 of them make a pound, which is why packaging often shows both.
Units of weight.Troy ounce: Precious metals are weighed in troy ounces, named after the French market town Troyes, and each is about 10 percent heavier than a regular ounce.
Units of weight.Pound: The abbreviation lb comes from Latin libra, the Roman scale, which is also why the pound sterling has its pound sign.
Units of weight.Stone: Britons still weigh themselves in stones, a unit that began as an actual stone used on market scales; 14 pounds make one.
Units of weight.Hundredweight (UK): The UK hundredweight is 112 pounds, not 100, which is why the American short hundredweight and this one are famously different.
Units of weight.Tonne: Also called the metric ton, a tonne is roughly the weight of a small car, and it is spelled this way to tell it from the imperial ton.

Dystopian novels, by publication year.Brave New World: Huxley's novel imagines a future where people are kept content with drugs and conditioning, and the title borrows from Shakespeare's The Tempest.
Dystopian novels, by publication year.Anthem: Ayn Rand's short novella is set in a future where the word I has been forgotten, and people only say we.
Dystopian novels, by publication year.Nineteen Eighty-Four: Orwell's book gave us Big Brother, doublethink and Room 101, and these terms are now widely used for any intrusive state.
Dystopian novels, by publication year.Fahrenheit 451: The title refers to the temperature at which paper burns, and Bradbury originally developed the story from shorter fiction.
Dystopian novels, by publication year.A Clockwork Orange: Anthony Burgess invented the slang Nadsat for this novel, mixing English with Russian words, and Kubrick's film made it famous.
Dystopian novels, by publication year.The Handmaid's Tale: Margaret Atwood has said that nothing in the book had not already happened somewhere, and its red robes became a protest symbol.
Dystopian novels, by publication year.The Giver: Lois Lowry's novel, aimed at young readers, won the Newbery Medal, and it is often taught in schools for its themes about memory and choice.
Dystopian novels, by publication year.Never Let Me Go: Kazuo Ishiguro's story unfolds quietly at a boarding school, and the author later won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 2017.
Dystopian novels, by publication year.The Road: Cormac McCarthy's bleak novel about a father and son in a ruined America won the Pulitzer Prize for fiction in 2007.
Dystopian novels, by publication year.The Hunger Games: Suzanne Collins reportedly got the idea while flipping between reality TV and war coverage, and the series sold tens of millions of copies.

Famous numbers from sports legends.Phelps's golds in Beijing: Michael Phelps won eight golds at the 2008 Beijing Games, breaking Mark Spitz's seven-gold record from 1972, with one race decided by a hundredth of a second.
Famous numbers from sports legends.Comaneci's famous score: Nadia Comaneci scored the first perfect 10 in Olympic gymnastics in 1976, and the scoreboard could only show 1.00 because it had not been built for that.
Famous numbers from sports legends.Marciano's pro wins: Rocky Marciano retired undefeated as heavyweight champion with 49 wins and no losses, and 43 of those wins came by knockout.
Famous numbers from sports legends.DiMaggio's hitting streak: Joe DiMaggio's 56-game hitting streak in 1941 is still unbroken, and many baseball experts regard it as the most unbreakable record in sport.
Famous numbers from sports legends.Bradman's Test average: Don Bradman's Test average is so far beyond everyone else, as no other long-career batsman has gotten close to 70, let alone 100.
Famous numbers from sports legends.Wilt's points in one game: Wilt Chamberlain scored 100 points in one NBA game in 1962, and no one has come close since; the game wasn't televised.
Famous numbers from sports legends.Babe Ruth's career homers: Babe Ruth hit 714 home runs, a record that stood for decades until Hank Aaron passed it in 1974.
Famous numbers from sports legends.Ripken's straight games: Cal Ripken Jr. played in 2,632 consecutive games, breaking Lou Gehrig's record, and earned the nickname Iron Man.
Famous numbers from sports legends.Pete Rose's career hits: Pete Rose collected 4,256 hits, passing Ty Cobb's record, though he was later banned from baseball over gambling.
Famous numbers from sports legends.Nolan Ryan's strikeouts: Nolan Ryan threw seven no-hitters and pitched until he was 46, and his strikeout record is considered nearly impossible to beat.

When these card games were released.Rook: Created by Parker Brothers as a game for people who avoided face-card decks, so it was popular in Mennonite and Amish communities.
When these card games were released.Uno: Invented by an Ohio barber, Merle Robbins, who reportedly developed it with his family. Mattel bought it in 1992 and now sells it worldwide.
When these card games were released.Phase 10: A rummy-style game in which you must complete ten set-and-run goals in order, so a bad hand early on can drag your whole game.
When these card games were released.Magic: The Gathering: The first trading card game, created by mathematician Richard Garfield. Single copies of the early Black Lotus card have sold for hundreds of thousands of dollars.
When these card games were released.Pokémon TCG: Launched in Japan alongside the video games. A promotional card called Pikachu Illustrator has sold for millions.
When these card games were released.Yu-Gi-Oh! TCG: Based on Kazuki Takahashi's manga, which featured a fictional card duel. The real game became one of the world's biggest trading card games.
When these card games were released.Dominion: Donald X. Vaccarino's game launched the deck-building genre: you start with a weak deck and build it up during play.
When these card games were released.Cards Against Humanity: It began as a Kickstarter by a group of Chicago friends, and the cards are free to download and print under a Creative Commons license.
When these card games were released.Hearthstone: Blizzard's digital card game set in the Warcraft universe. It showed that online-only card games could rival physical ones.
When these card games were released.Exploding Kittens: It raised record-setting funds on Kickstarter in 2015, becoming the platform's most-backed project at that time.

Southern Hemisphere cities from north to.Nairobi: It sits at 1.3 degrees south, almost on the equator, yet its altitude keeps it cool and gives it a mild climate.
Southern Hemisphere cities from north to.Jakarta: Once called Batavia under Dutch rule, it is now one of the largest cities in the world and is slowly sinking.
Southern Hemisphere cities from north to.Lima: Rain is scarce in this desert city on the Pacific coast, and a thick sea fog called garua covers it in winter.
Southern Hemisphere cities from north to.La Paz: It is an altitude capital with a cable car network, Mi Teleferico, the highest and longest urban one in the world.
Southern Hemisphere cities from north to.Rio de Janeiro: The Christ the Redeemer statue stands on Corcovado peak above the city, and was named one of the new Seven Wonders of the World.
Southern Hemisphere cities from north to.Johannesburg: Founded in 1886 after a gold rush, it is one of the largest cities not located on a coast, river or lake.
Southern Hemisphere cities from north to.Durban: It is home to a large South African Indian community, and the city's curry, the bunny chow, was created here.
Southern Hemisphere cities from north to.Buenos Aires: Tango was born in its port neighborhoods in the late 1800s, a mix of immigrant and local music.
Southern Hemisphere cities from north to.Punta Arenas: It lies on the Strait of Magellan, which Ferdinand Magellan sailed through in 1520, and was long a port for ships rounding South America.
Southern Hemisphere cities from north to.Ushuaia: Often called the southernmost city on Earth, nicknamed End of the World, it is a gateway to Antarctica.

Wizarding World books, by publication.Philosopher's Stone: Rejected by about a dozen publishers, it first had a print run of just 500 copies, 300 of which went to libraries.
Wizarding World books, by publication.Chamber of Secrets: This book introduced Dobby the house-elf and the diary of Tom Riddle, revealing the history of the Chamber.
Wizarding World books, by publication.Prisoner of Azkaban: It is the only book in the series where Voldemort never appears in person.
Wizarding World books, by publication.Goblet of Fire: Nearly twice as long as the first book, it marks the series' darker turn and introduces the Triwizard Tournament.
Wizarding World books, by publication.Fantastic Beasts (textbook): Written as if by Newt Scamander, it was published for the charity Comic Relief and raised millions for children in need.
Wizarding World books, by publication.Order of the Phoenix: At 766 pages in its UK edition, it is the longest book in the series.
Wizarding World books, by publication.Half-Blood Prince: It sold around nine million copies in its first 24 hours across the UK and US, in the summer of 2005.
Wizarding World books, by publication.Deathly Hallows: It sold about 15 million copies in its first day, making it the fastest-selling book up to that point.
Wizarding World books, by publication.The Tales of Beedle the Bard: Rowling hand-wrote seven copies, and one sold at auction for about 1.95 million pounds in 2007, before a charity edition appeared.
Wizarding World books, by publication.The Cursed Child (script): The stage script by Jack Thorne comes from a story by him, Rowling and director John Tiffany, and set in the adult years of Harry.

Transistor counts of famous chips.Intel 4004: Intel's first microprocessor was built for a Busicom calculator, and it sits in a chip smaller than your thumbnail.
Transistor counts of famous chips.Intel 8086: This 16-bit chip gave its name to the x86 instruction set, which still underlies most PCs.
Transistor counts of famous chips.Intel 386: Intel's first 32-bit x86 processor, it made modern multitasking operating systems practical on PCs.
Transistor counts of famous chips.Intel 486: It was the first x86 chip to put a built-in floating-point unit and cache on the same die as the CPU.
Transistor counts of famous chips.Intel Pentium: Intel named it Pentium because a plain number could not be trademarked; it is also remembered for a 1994 division bug.
Transistor counts of famous chips.Pentium 4 (Willamette): It launched around 1.5 GHz; Intel's NetBurst design chased clock speed at the cost of efficiency.
Transistor counts of famous chips.Core 2 Duo (Conroe): Its two cores marked Intel's return to efficiency after the heat-hungry Pentium 4 era.
Transistor counts of famous chips.Apple M1: Apple's first Mac chip was built on a 5 nm process, putting CPU, GPU and memory together in one package.
Transistor counts of famous chips.Apple M1 Max: This chip fuses a huge GPU with up to 64 GB of shared memory, aimed at video and creative professionals.
Transistor counts of famous chips.Nvidia H100: Nvidia's AI accelerator, on the Hopper design named for computing pioneer Grace Hopper, is built for training large models.

Heights of great churches and temples.Pantheon, Rome: The Roman temple's unreinforced concrete dome, completed around 126 AD, is still the largest of its kind. Its open oculus is 8 meters wide.
Heights of great churches and temples.Hagia Sophia: Built in Constantinople in 537 as a cathedral, then a mosque, museum and mosque again. Its huge dome was the world's largest for nearly a thousand years.
Heights of great churches and temples.Notre-Dame de Paris (spire): The 2019 fire destroyed its famous spire, which was a 19th-century addition. Its reopened interior drew crowds in late 2024.
Heights of great churches and temples.St. Paul's Cathedral: Christopher Wren designed it after the Great Fire of London. Its dome was the tallest in the city for centuries and survived the Blitz.
Heights of great churches and temples.Salisbury Cathedral: Its spire, added in the 1300s, is the tallest church spire in Britain. The cathedral also keeps one of four surviving copies of Magna Carta.
Heights of great churches and temples.St. Peter's Basilica: The world's largest church, with a dome partly designed by Michelangelo. Its Renaissance building replaced an older basilica from the 4th century.
Heights of great churches and temples.Strasbourg Cathedral: It was the tallest building in the world from 1647, when its spire was finished, until 1874. Its astronomical clock is a famed attraction.
Heights of great churches and temples.Rouen Cathedral: Monet painted its facade over 30 times in changing light. Its cast-iron spire, finished in 1876, briefly made it the tallest building in the world.
Heights of great churches and temples.Cologne Cathedral: Building took more than 600 years, from 1248 to 1880. It survived the bombing of World War II and was the tallest building in the world until 1884.
Heights of great churches and temples.Ulm Minster: Its tower is the tallest church steeple in the world. Construction ran from 1377, and the spire was finally completed in 1890.

Pro boxing weight class limits.Minimumweight: Also called strawweight, this lowest division is capped at 105 pounds, about 47.6 kg, and was created in the 1980s for the smallest fighters.
Pro boxing weight class limits.Flyweight: Welsh legend Jimmy Wilde, "the Ghost with a Hammer", ruled this 112-pound class in the 1910s despite looking frail, and won over 130 fights.
Pro boxing weight class limits.Bantamweight: The 118-pound class is named for the bantam chicken, a small breed known for being feisty and unafraid of larger birds.
Pro boxing weight class limits.Featherweight: The 126-pound class once crowned Naseem Hamed, the flamboyant British "Prince" who vaulted into the ring for his entrances.
Pro boxing weight class limits.Lightweight: Roberto Duran, "Hands of Stone", won his first world title at 135 pounds in 1972, then went on to win titles in four weight classes.
Pro boxing weight class limits.Welterweight: At 147 pounds, this division featured Sugar Ray Leonard and Floyd Mayweather, and many say Sugar Ray Robinson began his greatness here.
Pro boxing weight class limits.Middleweight: Marvelous Marvin Hagler held the undisputed 160-pound title for about seven years in the 1980s, defending it a dozen times.
Pro boxing weight class limits.Super middleweight: This 168-pound division was created in the 1980s. Joe Calzaghe of Wales held a world title here for a decade and retired unbeaten.
Pro boxing weight class limits.Light heavyweight: At 175 pounds, Archie Moore, nicknamed "the Old Mongoose", held the title for nearly a decade and is said to have fought into his late forties.
Pro boxing weight class limits.Cruiserweight: Introduced in 1979 at 190 pounds, the division was later raised to 200 pounds. Evander Holyfield was cruiserweight champion before moving to heavyweight.

Coaching legends, by start of their famo.John Wooden at UCLA: UCLA's "Wizard of Westwood" won ten NCAA titles in 12 years, and is also known for his "Pyramid of Success" philosophy.
Coaching legends, by start of their famo.Red Auerbach at the Celtics: The Boston Celtics coach famously lit a victory cigar when he felt a game was won, and led the team to nine titles, eight in a row.
Coaching legends, by start of their famo.Vince Lombardi at Green Bay: Coach of the Green Bay Packers, he won five NFL championships, including the first two Super Bowls, and the trophy is named after him.
Coaching legends, by start of their famo.Rinus Michels at Ajax: The Dutch coach created "Total Football" at Ajax, a style based on fluid positions, which inspired Barcelona's style and Johan Cruyff.
Coaching legends, by start of their famo.Alex Ferguson at Man United: Manchester United's boss for over 26 years, he won 13 Premier League titles, and a record 38 trophies before retiring in 2013.
Coaching legends, by start of their famo.Phil Jackson at the Bulls: Led the Bulls to six NBA championships in the 1990s with stars Michael Jordan and Scottie Pippen, and later won more with the Lakers.
Coaching legends, by start of their famo.Arsene Wenger at Arsenal: The Frenchman took over at Arsenal in 1996 and led them to an unbeaten Premier League season in 2003-04, the "Invincibles".
Coaching legends, by start of their famo.Bill Belichick at the Patriots: New England's coach, who led the Patriots to six Super Bowl wins with quarterback Tom Brady.
Coaching legends, by start of their famo.Pep Guardiola at Barcelona: In his first season in charge, 2008-09, Barcelona won La Liga, the Copa del Rey and the Champions League, a treble no Spanish club had managed.
Coaching legends, by start of their famo.Jurgen Klopp at Liverpool: The German coach took over at Liverpool in 2015, won the Champions League in 2019 and the club's first league title in 30 years in 2020.

When these countries joined NATO.Canada: The North American nation was a founding member, and it helped create the alliance in Washington in 1949.
When these countries joined NATO.Turkey: The country joined along with Greece, and it controls the Bosphorus Strait, and has the second-largest army in NATO.
When these countries joined NATO.West Germany: The country was admitted a decade after the war, and the Soviets responded by forming the Warsaw Pact.
When these countries joined NATO.Spain: The country joined after the death of Franco, and it voted to stay in a referendum in 1986.
When these countries joined NATO.Poland: This former Warsaw Pact country joined with Hungary and the Czech Republic, and it is now one of the biggest military spenders in the alliance.
When these countries joined NATO.Estonia: This Baltic state shares a border with Russia, and it is known for its digital government and e-residency.
When these countries joined NATO.Albania: The Balkan country joined together with Croatia, and it is known for its 'country of eagles' nickname.
When these countries joined NATO.Montenegro: The small Balkan country was admitted despite Russian objections, and it declared independence from Serbia in 2006.
When these countries joined NATO.North Macedonia: It changed its name from Macedonia after an agreement with Greece, which had blocked its entry.
When these countries joined NATO.Finland: After the invasion of Ukraine, the Nordic country dropped its long neutrality, and it has the longest border with Russia of any member.

When each country's first high-speed rai.Japan's Shinkansen: It opened days before the 1964 Tokyo Olympics, and the network has never had a passenger fatality from derailment or collision.
When each country's first high-speed rai.France's TGV: A TGV set the rail speed record of 574.8 km/h on a test run in 2007.
When each country's first high-speed rai.Germany's ICE: It launched in 1991 with the Hannover–Würzburg line, linking cities long divided by the Cold War.
When each country's first high-speed rai.Spain's AVE: AVE stands for Alta Velocidad Española and also means 'bird' in Spanish, a neat pun; its first line opened for Expo 92.
When each country's first high-speed rai.USA's Acela: Running Boston to Washington, it is limited by old track, so it rarely reaches the speeds the trains were designed for.
When each country's first high-speed rai.South Korea's KTX: It started in 2004 using French TGV technology, making Korea an Asian high-speed pioneer.
When each country's first high-speed rai.Taiwan High Speed Rail: Running down the island's west coast, it uses Japanese Shinkansen technology.
When each country's first high-speed rai.China's Beijing–Tianjin line: Opened just before the 2008 Beijing Olympics; China now has more high-speed track than the rest of the world combined.
When each country's first high-speed rai.Turkey's YHT: Its initials stand for Yüksek Hızlı Tren, 'high-speed train', and the first line linked Ankara and Eskişehir.
When each country's first high-speed rai.Morocco's Al Boraq: Africa's first high-speed line links Tangier and Casablanca, and 'Al Boraq' is the winged steed of Islamic tradition.

How much one of these eggs weighs.Caviar (one sturgeon egg): Strictly speaking, only sturgeon roe is caviar, and some sturgeon take well over a decade to mature enough to produce it.
How much one of these eggs weighs.Salmon roe (one egg): Called ikura in Japanese sushi, from the Russian word for roe. The bright orange eggs burst when you bite them.
How much one of these eggs weighs.Quail egg: Their speckled shells are a common topping in Japanese cooking, and each hen's markings differ.
How much one of these eggs weighs.Pigeon egg: Pigeons lay only two eggs at a time, and both parents feed the chicks 'crop milk'.
How much one of these eggs weighs.Chicken egg: A hen lays up to around 300 a year, and each shell has thousands of tiny pores that let the chick breathe.
How much one of these eggs weighs.Duck egg: Prized by bakers for its richer yolk, and salted duck eggs are a Chinese staple.
How much one of these eggs weighs.Turkey egg: Rarely sold in shops, because turkeys lay far fewer eggs than chickens.
How much one of these eggs weighs.Goose egg: Geese lay mostly in spring, and each egg is roughly three chicken eggs' worth.
How much one of these eggs weighs.Emu egg: Dark green and thick-shelled. The male incubates for about eight weeks and eats very little in that time.
How much one of these eggs weighs.Ostrich egg: The biggest egg of any living bird, equal to about two dozen chicken eggs, yet the smallest relative to its mother's size.

Middle East and Africa from north to sou.Istanbul: It straddles two continents across the Bosphorus, and was successively named Byzantium, Constantinople and Istanbul.
Middle East and Africa from north to sou.Baghdad: Founded in 762 as the Abbasid 'City of Peace', it became the center of Islam's Golden Age, with a House of Wisdom.
Middle East and Africa from north to sou.Jerusalem: Sacred to Jews, Christians and Muslims, its Old City packs the Western Wall, Church of the Holy Sepulchre and Dome of the Rock into one square kilometer.
Middle East and Africa from north to sou.Kuwait City: The Gulf capital is a city-state at heart, and its skyline is dominated by the Kuwait Towers, with oil underpinning its wealth.
Middle East and Africa from north to sou.Riyadh: A Saudi capital in the middle of the desert, it began as an oasis village, and its name means 'the gardens'.
Middle East and Africa from north to sou.Khartoum: Where the Blue and White Nile meet, the city's name may come from the Arabic word for an elephant's trunk.
Middle East and Africa from north to sou.Lagos: Nigeria's biggest city is one of the world's fastest-growing, and it's the heart of Nollywood.
Middle East and Africa from north to sou.Kampala: Uganda's hilly capital sits almost on the equator, and Lake Victoria is just to its south.
Middle East and Africa from north to sou.Harare: Formerly Salisbury, renamed Harare in 1982, it sits on a plateau about 1,500 m up, which keeps its climate pleasantly mild.
Middle East and Africa from north to sou.Cape Town: Beneath Table Mountain at Africa's southwestern tip, it's among the most scenic cities on earth, near the Cape of Good Hope.

Electric cars, by first delivery year.GM EV1: GM's EV1 was leased, not sold, to drivers in California, and the company recalled and crushed most of them.
Electric cars, by first delivery year.Tesla Roadster: The first mass-produced electric car using lithium-ion cells, it was based on the Lotus Elise and proved electric cars could be fast.
Electric cars, by first delivery year.Nissan Leaf: One of the best-selling electric cars ever, its name comes from LEAF, an acronym of the leading, environmentally friendly, affordable family car.
Electric cars, by first delivery year.BMW i3: BMW's carbon-fiber city car, which has an optional range-extending engine, and it was a bold design for its day.
Electric cars, by first delivery year.Chevrolet Bolt: Chevy's affordable electric hatchback was later recalled over battery fire risks, and the company replaced the packs.
Electric cars, by first delivery year.Tesla Model 3: It took the Tesla brand to the mass market, and by the early 2020s had become among the best-selling cars in the world.
Electric cars, by first delivery year.Porsche Taycan: Porsche's first all-electric sports car, which can charge extremely fast thanks to an 800-volt system.
Electric cars, by first delivery year.Ford Mustang Mach-E: Ford put the Mustang name on an electric SUV, which upset some purists, but it sold well.
Electric cars, by first delivery year.Rivian R1T: This electric pickup, from a startup, was first to market ahead of Ford and Tesla's trucks, with a built-in camping kitchen option.
Electric cars, by first delivery year.Tesla Cybertruck: Its angular stainless-steel body was famously shown with a window that cracked on stage during its 2019 unveiling.

Light and radio by wavelength.Gamma rays: The most energetic light, gamma rays come from nuclear reactions and exploding stars, and they pass through most materials.
Light and radio by wavelength.X-rays: Wilhelm Röntgen found them in 1895 and photographed his wife's hand, the first X-ray image of a person.
Light and radio by wavelength.Ultraviolet: Invisible to us but visible to bees, it also causes sunburn, and is mostly filtered out by the ozone layer.
Light and radio by wavelength.Blue light: The color of the daytime sky, blue light scatters more than red, which is why the sky isn't violet to our eyes.
Light and radio by wavelength.Red light: The longest wavelength we can see, red is where the visible spectrum ends, and it is at the edge of sunset colors.
Light and radio by wavelength.Body-heat infrared: People radiate it, which is why night-vision cameras can see warm bodies in the dark.
Light and radio by wavelength.Cosmic microwave peak: The faint afterglow of the Big Bang was first picked up in the mid-1960s by two radio engineers who even checked pigeon droppings as the cause.
Light and radio by wavelength.Hydrogen's spin-flip line: Hydrogen atoms emit this radio wave, and radio astronomers use it to map our galaxy's gas.
Light and radio by wavelength.FM radio: Its waves are a few meters long, and the signals carry music with less static than AM, but have shorter range.
Light and radio by wavelength.AM radio: The longest waves here can bend around hills and travel far at night by bouncing off the ionosphere.

Physics breakthroughs of the 20th centur.Planck's quanta: Max Planck proposed that energy comes in tiny packets, a reluctant fix for glowing-object physics that launched quantum theory.
Physics breakthroughs of the 20th centur.Atomic nucleus: Rutherford's team fired particles at gold foil and some bounced back, revealing that each atom has a tiny, dense core.
Physics breakthroughs of the 20th centur.Bohr's model of the atom: Niels Bohr proposed that electrons orbit only at fixed energy levels, jumping between them by absorbing or emitting light.
Physics breakthroughs of the 20th centur.General relativity: Einstein recast gravity as curved spacetime; it explained Mercury's odd orbit and predicted starlight bending, confirmed in 1919.
Physics breakthroughs of the 20th centur.Schrödinger equation: Erwin Schrödinger's wave equation describes how quantum systems evolve and underlies modern chemistry and electronics.
Physics breakthroughs of the 20th centur.Expanding universe (Hubble): Edwin Hubble found that distant galaxies recede faster the farther away they are, showing that the universe is expanding.
Physics breakthroughs of the 20th centur.Nuclear fission: Hahn and Strassmann split uranium atoms in Berlin, and Lise Meitner and Otto Frisch explained the result and named it fission.
Physics breakthroughs of the 20th centur.First laser: Theodore Maiman built it with a flash lamp and a ruby crystal; lasers now run barcode scanners, surgery and fiber internet.
Physics breakthroughs of the 20th centur.Bose-Einstein condensate: Atoms cooled to near absolute zero merged into a single quantum 'super atom'; Cornell, Wieman and Ketterle won a Nobel for it.
Physics breakthroughs of the 20th centur.First image of a black hole: The Event Horizon Telescope linked radio dishes across the globe to photograph the glowing ring around the black hole in galaxy M87.

How high above Earth's surface.Cruising airliner: Outside, the air is around minus 55 degrees Celsius, but the cabin is pressurised so passengers sit comfortably.
How high above Earth's surface.Felix Baumgartner's jump: The 2012 Red Bull Stratos jump reached roughly 1,350 km/h, and he became the first person to break the sound barrier in free fall.
How high above Earth's surface.Kármán line (edge of space): It is named after physicist Theodore von Kármán, who worked out that wings can't fly in air that thin.
How high above Earth's surface.International Space Station: The station orbits Earth about every 90 minutes, so its crew sees roughly 16 sunrises and sunsets every day.
How high above Earth's surface.Hubble Space Telescope: After launch in 1990 it needed spectacles: astronauts installed corrective optics in 1993 to fix its flawed mirror.
How high above Earth's surface.GPS satellites: Each satellite orbits twice a day, and its clocks need relativity corrections or GPS positions would drift by kilometres daily.
How high above Earth's surface.Geostationary satellites: Arthur C. Clarke described this orbit in 1945, where a satellite matches Earth's spin and seems to hover over a spot.
How high above Earth's surface.The Moon: The Moon is drifting away from us by about 3.8 cm per year, measured by bouncing lasers off reflectors left by Apollo.
How high above Earth's surface.James Webb Space Telescope: Webb sits near a gravity balance point beyond the Moon, and its sunshield is about the size of a tennis court.
How high above Earth's surface.The Sun: Its light takes just over eight minutes to reach us, and the distance defines the astronomical unit.

Movie stars by birth year.Marlon Brando: The method actor revolutionised screen acting, and famously refused his Oscar for The Godfather.
Movie stars by birth year.Clint Eastwood: The actor and director won Best Director for Unforgiven, and later won again for Million Dollar Baby.
Movie stars by birth year.Jack Nicholson: He earned 12 Oscar nominations, the most of any male actor, and won three.
Movie stars by birth year.Meryl Streep: She has received more Oscar nominations than any other actor, over 20, and has won three.
Movie stars by birth year.Denzel Washington: He won Oscars for Glory and Training Day, among the few actors with a win in both categories.
Movie stars by birth year.Tom Hanks: He won back-to-back Best Actor Oscars for Philadelphia and Forrest Gump.
Movie stars by birth year.Tom Cruise: He performs many of his own stunts, including hanging off the Burj Khalifa for Mission: Impossible.
Movie stars by birth year.Leonardo DiCaprio: He finally won an Oscar for The Revenant, after years of nominations.
Movie stars by birth year.Emma Stone: She was born Emily and adopted Emma because another Emily Stone was already registered with the actors' union.
Movie stars by birth year.Zendaya: She won a lead actress Emmy for Euphoria at 24, making her the youngest winner in that category.

When these Nintendo series debuted.Duck Hunt: The famous NES light gun, the Zapper, was used in it, and the mocking dog became icon.
When these Nintendo series debuted.Mother (EarthBound): Released in Japan, the first game was later followed by Mother 2, which was renamed EarthBound for Western audiences.
When these Nintendo series debuted.F-Zero: Launched with the Super Famicom, it used Mode 7 scaling for a feeling of speed, with Captain Falcon.
When these Nintendo series debuted.Star Fox: It used a special Super FX chip on the SNES to render 3D polygons.
Masahiro Sakurai first built a prototype with plain characters, which became Nintendo's biggest crossover.
When these Nintendo series debuted.Animal Crossing: It began on the Nintendo 64 in Japan as Dobutsu no Mori, and uses the console's real-time clock.
When these Nintendo series debuted.Nintendogs: A puppy simulator for the DS that used the microphone to call dogs by name.
When these Nintendo series debuted.Wii Fit: It came with a Balance Board and sold over 22 million copies.
When these Nintendo series debuted.Splatoon: Nintendo's new ink-shooter franchise on Wii U, with squid-kid characters.
When these Nintendo series debuted.ARMS: A Switch fighting game with boxers whose springy extending arms are controlled by motion.

Spectacles in Earth's skies through hist.Crab supernova seen: Chinese astronomers recorded a 'guest star', and its remains are the Crab Nebula.
Spectacles in Earth's skies through hist.Tycho's supernova: Tycho Brahe's observation showed the heavens could change, because the new star showed no shift against the stars.
Spectacles in Earth's skies through hist.Kepler's supernova: It is the last supernova seen in our Milky Way by the naked eye.
Spectacles in Earth's skies through hist.Great Leonid meteor storm: Tens of thousands of shooting stars an hour fell in this storm, and it sparked modern meteor science.
Spectacles in Earth's skies through hist.Tunguska explosion: A cosmic explosion above Siberia flattened some 80 million trees over about 2,000 square kilometres.
Spectacles in Earth's skies through hist.Earth passes Halley's tail: Earth passed through the comet's tail, and some people bought anti-comet pills out of panic.
Spectacles in Earth's skies through hist.Supernova in the LMC: The closest supernova seen in centuries, its neutrinos reached detectors on Earth.
Spectacles in Earth's skies through hist.Shoemaker-Levy 9 hits Jupiter: The comet, broken into pieces, slammed into Jupiter in the first direct observation of such a collision.
Spectacles in Earth's skies through hist.Chelyabinsk meteor: The meteor exploded over Russia, and the shock wave shattered windows and injured about 1,500 people.
Spectacles in Earth's skies through hist.'Oumuamua discovered: The first known interstellar visitor passed through, and its Hawaiian name means 'scout' or 'messenger'.

Turning points in Indian history.First Battle of Panipat: Babur's army used gunpowder and cannons to defeat the Sultan of Delhi here. It founded the Mughal Empire, which ruled for over 300 years.
Turning points in Indian history.Work begins on the Taj Mahal: Shah Jahan began building the monument for his wife Mumtaz Mahal. It took about 20 years and thousands of workers.
Turning points in Indian history.Battle of Plassey: Robert Clive's East India Company forces beat the Nawab of Bengal, helped by a commander's betrayal. It started British rule over much of India.
Turning points in Indian history.Indian Rebellion: Sparked by Indian soldiers in the Company's army, this uprising spread across northern India. Afterwards the Crown took direct control.
Turning points in Indian history.Indian National Congress born: Founded in Bombay with help from a retired British official, Allan Octavian Hume. It became the main force in the independence movement.
Turning points in Indian history.Amritsar massacre: British troops under General Dyer fired on an unarmed crowd at Jallianwala Bagh in Amritsar. It hardened Indian opinion against British rule.
Turning points in Indian history.Gandhi's Salt March: Gandhi walked about 240 miles to the coast at Dandi to make salt in defiance of the British tax. It gathered thousands of followers.
Turning points in Indian history.Independence and Partition: India became independent on 15 August 1947, and British India was divided into India and Pakistan. Millions were displaced.
Turning points in Indian history.Indira Gandhi's Emergency: Indira Gandhi suspended civil liberties for 21 months and jailed opponents. She lost the election that followed in 1977.
Turning points in Indian history.Pokhran-II nuclear tests: India detonated five devices in the Rajasthan desert, under the code name Operation Shakti. Pakistan answered with its own tests weeks later.

Winter Olympic host cities from north to.Lillehammer: Edvard Munch's The Scream was stolen from an Oslo museum on the opening day of the 1994 Games.
Winter Olympic host cities from north to.Oslo: The 1952 Games' torch was lit in the home of Sondre Norheim, the father of modern skiing.
Winter Olympic host cities from north to.Calgary: The 1988 Games inspired Cool Runnings, about the Jamaican bobsled team.
Winter Olympic host cities from north to.Vancouver: The 2010 Games ran short of snow at Cypress Mountain, so organizers trucked and helicoptered it in.
Winter Olympic host cities from north to.Innsbruck: It hosted the Winter Games in 1964 and again in 1976, after Denver withdrew.
Winter Olympic host cities from north to.Turin: The 2006 Games were held in the home of Fiat and the Shroud of Turin.
Winter Olympic host cities from north to.Sapporo: The 1972 Games were the first Winter Games held in Asia, where Japan swept the 70 m ski jump podium.
Winter Olympic host cities from north to.Salt Lake City: It was awarded the 2034 Games, to reuse the venues from 2002.
Winter Olympic host cities from north to.Beijing: It is the first city to host both the Summer and Winter Games, in 2008 and 2022.
Winter Olympic host cities from north to.Pyeongchang: The 2018 Games were South Korea's first, and North and South marched under one flag.

Sleeps, real and storybook, by length.Microsleep: These brief lapses of sleep happen when you are very tired, and the person often does not realise. They are a major cause of drowsy-driving crashes.
Sleeps, real and storybook, by length.Power nap: A short nap of about 20 minutes boosts alertness without deep sleep, so you avoid grogginess. Many famous people are said to have used them.
Sleeps, real and storybook, by length.One sleep cycle: A night's rest runs through repeating cycles of light, deep and REM sleep. Most vivid dreams happen in REM, when your muscles are mostly paralysed.
Sleeps, real and storybook, by length.A good night's sleep: Most adults need seven to nine hours. Sleep helps the brain store memories and clear away waste built up during the day.
Sleeps, real and storybook, by length.Newborn baby's daily sleep: Newborns sleep for most of the day but in short bursts, since their body clock has not yet developed. It takes a few months to settle into a day-night rhythm.
Sleeps, real and storybook, by length.Koala's daily sleep: Koalas sleep so long because their eucalyptus diet is low in energy and hard to digest. They're awake only a few hours each day.
Sleeps, real and storybook, by length.Hedgehog's hibernation: In winter its heart rate and breathing drop dramatically, and body temperature falls close to that of its surroundings, helping it survive without food.
Sleeps, real and storybook, by length.Dormouse's hibernation: The hazel dormouse spends more than half its life asleep. The Dormouse at the Mad Hatter's tea party in Alice in Wonderland is also forever nodding off.
Sleeps, real and storybook, by length.Rip Van Winkle's nap: Washington Irving's 1819 tale tells of a man who naps in the Catskills and wakes to find that two decades, and a revolution, have passed.
Sleeps, real and storybook, by length.Sleeping Beauty's sleep: In the fairy tale, a spindle prick sends the princess into a hundred-year sleep that only a kiss can break. Charles Perrault published the best-known version in 1697.

Making jam, step by step.Pick ripe fruit: Slightly underripe fruit has more pectin, the natural gel-maker, so jam makers often mix ripe and just-ripe berries for a good set.
Making jam, step by step.Wash and hull it: Hulling removes the green stem and leafy top from fruit like strawberries. It is fiddly work, but it improves the texture of the jam.
Making jam, step by step.Chop it up: Smaller pieces release juice and pectin more easily. Some jam makers mash fruit partly and leave other bits whole for texture.
Making jam, step by step.Simmer until soft: Gentle cooking softens the fruit and releases its pectin before the sugar goes in. Fruits like apples and citrus are rich in pectin.
Making jam, step by step.Stir in the sugar: Sugar is a preservative as well as a sweetener, because it draws water out of microbes. Dissolving it fully first prevents grainy jam.
Making jam, step by step.Boil hard: A rolling boil drives off water and reaches the setting point, around 105 degrees Celsius. This stage needs watching, as it can burn quickly.
Making jam, step by step.Wrinkle test on a cold plate: Drop a spoonful on a chilled plate, wait, and push it with a finger. If the surface wrinkles, the jam will set when cooled.
Making jam, step by step.Pour into hot jars: Sterilised jars and hot jam help prevent contamination. A funnel keeps the rims clean, and leaving a small gap at the top allows for a good seal.
Making jam, step by step.Seal the lids: As the jam cools, it contracts and pulls the lid down, creating a vacuum. Many lids have a button that pops down to show a good seal.
Making jam, step by step.Spread on toast: Jam made with whole fruit and sugar dates back centuries. In Britain, the thick marmalade made from Seville oranges is a classic breakfast spread.

The Lion King, in story order.Simba shown from Pride Rock: The Lion King (1994) opens with Circle of Life, and its story is often compared to Hamlet.
The Lion King, in story order.Mufasa shows Simba the kingdom: James Earl Jones, who voiced Mufasa, was also the voice of Darth Vader in Star Wars.
The Lion King, in story order.Hyenas chase Simba and Nala: Spotted hyenas live in female-led clans, where females are larger and in charge, though the film shows them as cowardly.
The Lion King, in story order.The wildebeest stampede: The wildebeest stampede used computer-generated animals to multiply the herd, a landmark for traditional animation.
The Lion King, in story order.Simba runs away: Simba is Swahili for lion, and other names follow suit: Rafiki is friend and Pumbaa is simpleton or foolish.
The Lion King, in story order.\"Hakuna Matata\": Hakuna matata is Swahili for no worries and became an everyday phrase after the film.
The Lion King, in story order.Nala finds grown-up Simba: Nala is Swahili for gift, and she was voiced as an adult by Moira Kelly.
The Lion King, in story order.Mufasa appears in the clouds: Mufasa's voice in the clouds tells Simba to remember who he is, and the line is among the film's best known.
The Lion King, in story order.Simba returns to Pride Rock: The film's landscape drew inspiration from Kenya, including Hell's Gate National Park.
The Lion King, in story order.Simba defeats Scar: Hyenas in reality are skilled hunters, not just scavengers, which the film's portrayal of them misses.

Macbeth, in story order.Witches greet Macbeth: The weird sisters speak in rhyming verse, like Double, double toil and trouble, as they brew their cauldron.
Macbeth, in story order.Made Thane of Cawdor: A thane was a Scottish noble title, and Cawdor Castle near Inverness still stands.
Macbeth, in story order.Macbeth murders Duncan: The real Macbeth was a Scottish king in the 11th century who killed Duncan in battle, not in his bed.
Macbeth, in story order.Macbeth is crowned: The crowning of Scottish kings took place at Scone, home of the Stone of Scone.
Macbeth, in story order.Banquo is murdered: Banquo's son Fleance escapes, and James I of England was said to descend from Banquo.
Macbeth, in story order.Banquo's ghost at the feast: Only Macbeth sees Banquo's ghost, a sign of his guilt and fraying mind.
Macbeth, in story order.Macduff's family is killed: Macduff was born by caesarean, which breaks the prophecy that no man born of woman can harm Macbeth.
Macbeth, in story order.Lady Macbeth sleepwalks: Lady Macbeth's Out, damned spot! comes as she sleepwalks, trying to wash invisible blood from her hands.
Macbeth, in story order.Birnam Wood comes to Dunsinane: Soldiers cut branches from Birnam Wood to hide their numbers, fulfilling the witches' prophecy.
Macbeth, in story order.Macduff kills Macbeth: Actors say the Scottish play instead of Macbeth in a theatre, thanks to a long-standing superstition.

Coffee through the centuries.Legend of Kaldi's goats: Said to be the story of an Ethiopian goatherd who noticed his goats dancing after eating coffee berries, first recorded centuries later.
Coffee through the centuries.First Venice coffeehouse: Coffee entered Europe through Venice's trade with the Ottomans, and legend says Pope Clement VIII approved after tasting it.
Coffee through the centuries.First English coffeehouse: In Oxford, coffeehouses were called penny universities because a penny bought coffee and conversation.
Coffee through the centuries.Lloyd's coffee house: Edward Lloyd's London coffee house became a hub for shipping insurers, and later Lloyd's of London.
Coffee through the centuries.Folgers founded: James Folger sold coffee to Gold Rush miners in San Francisco.
Coffee through the centuries.Maxwell House: Named after Nashville's Maxwell House Hotel; Teddy Roosevelt reportedly said it was good to the last drop.
Coffee through the centuries.Satori Kato's instant coffee: A Japanese chemist in Chicago invented soluble coffee powder.
Coffee through the centuries.Nescafé: Nestle created it to deal with Brazil's coffee surplus, and Allied soldiers drank it in World War II.
Coffee through the centuries.Starbucks opens: Opened in Pike Place Market in Seattle, and named after the first mate in Moby-Dick.
Coffee through the centuries.Keurig K-Cup: The pods launched for offices before homes, and inventor John Sylvan has said he regrets the waste.
